facts.statement: The genus Kryptodrakon was named and described by Andres, Clark, and Xu in 2014.
facts.quote: authority: Andres, Clark & Xu, 2014

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Kryptodrakon progenitor.
facts.quote: type_species: Kryptodrakon progenitor

facts.statement: Kryptodrakon lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic, approximately 162.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Kryptodrakon is an extinct genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Middle to Late Jurassic with an age of approximately 162.7 million years.

facts.statement: Kryptodrakon is the oldest and most basal known pterodactyloid.
facts.quote: The age of its fossil remains made Kryptodrakon the basalmost and oldest pterodactyloid known to date.

facts.statement: Fossil bones of Kryptodrakon were discovered in Xinjiang in 2001 by Chris Sloan.
facts.quote: In 2001, pterosaur bones were discovered in Xinjiang by Chris Sloan.

facts.statement: The fossils were initially mistaken for a theropod dinosaur before James Clark identified them as a pterosaur.
facts.quote: The bones were first identified as those of a theropod; paleontologist James Clark later recognized their pterosaurian nature.

facts.statement: Brian Andres, James Clark, and Xu Xing formally named the species Kryptodrakon progenitor in 2014.
facts.quote: In 2014, Brian Andres, Clark and Xu Xing named and described the type species Kryptodrakon progenitor.

facts.statement: The generic name Kryptodrakon means 'hidden dragon' in Greek.
facts.quote: The generic name means hidden dragon from Greek κρυπτός, kryptos (hidden), and δράκων, drakon (dragon).

facts.statement: The name alludes to the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, which was filmed near the fossil site.
facts.quote: The name alludes to the film Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, which included some scenes filmed near the type locality.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to the Callovian–Oxfordian stages with a minimum age of 161 million years.
facts.quote: The holotype, IVPP V18184, was uncovered in a layer of the Shishugou Formation dating from the Callovian–Oxfordian and having a minimum age of 161 million years.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of various wing and shoulder bones, including parts of the humerus, radius, metacarpals, and wing phalanges.
facts.quote: It consists of: a partial sacrum; the ventral ramus of the left coracoid; the anterior end of the right scapulocoracoid; the proximal end and shaft of the left humerus; the distal end of right radius; the right distal syncarpal; the right prexial carpal; a right metacarpal; the proximal end of the right first wing phalanx; the proximal end and shaft of the left second wing phalanx; the shaft of the right third wing phalanx and the proximal end of right fourth wing phalanx.

facts.statement: The bones were found unarticulated in a small 30 cm² area, likely representing a single individual.
facts.quote: The bones were not articulated but were discovered in a small area of 30 cm2, at a considerable distance from other fossil remains, and thus likely represent a single individual.

facts.statement: Kryptodrakon had an estimated wingspan of 1.47 meters.
facts.quote: Kryptodrakon has an estimated wingspan of 1.47 m.

facts.statement: Kryptodrakon's slender and elongated fourth metacarpal indicates it is a pterodactyloid.
facts.quote: Its fourth metacarpal is relatively slender and elongated, a strong indication that Kryptodrakon is a pterodactyloid.

facts.statement: The fourth metacarpal is at least 7.22 cm long, while the humerus is estimated to be between 7.5 cm and 8.6 cm.
facts.quote: The fourth metacarpal has a minimum length of 7.22 cm, while the humerus has an estimated length of between 7.5 cm and 8.6 cm.

facts.statement: The radius has a unique feature: an extra lump on its front outer lower side.
facts.quote: The radius shows an autapomorphy: it possesses an extra lump on the front outer lower side.

facts.statement: The skeleton shows no signs of pneumatization.
facts.quote: The skeleton shows no signs of pneumatization.

facts.statement: Kryptodrakon is approximately five million years older than previously discovered pterodactyloids.
facts.quote: The species is about five million years older than the oldest pterodactyloids previously discovered.

facts.statement: It is debated whether a previously described Middle Jurassic jaw from the UK is a pterosaur or a teleosaurid stem-crocodilian.
facts.quote: A supposedly older pterodactyloid, a partial jaw referred to the group Ctenochasmatidae, had been described from the Middle Jurassic of the UK. However, this specimen probably represents a teleosaurid stem-crocodilian instead of a pterosaur.

facts.statement: Kryptodrakon lived in a terrestrial habitat far from the coast.
facts.quote: Kryptodrakon lived in a terrestrial or in-land habitat, far from the coast.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Kryptodrakon's terrestrial habitat indicates a terrestrial origin for the Pterodactyloidea.
facts.quote: Andres and colleagues saw this as an indication that the Pterodactyloidea had a terrestrial origin.

facts.statement: The relatively short wings of Kryptodrakon support the hypothesis that short-winged species inhabit forests while long-winged species live near coasts.
facts.quote: The relatively short wings of Kryptodrakon confirm this hypothesis, as long-winged species of modern birds and long-winged pterosaurs tend to live at the coast and short-winged species tend to inhabit forests, as was shown by a study published as part of the describing article.

facts.statement: Kryptodrakon lived from 161.5 to 154.8 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 154.8 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The specific name progenitor means 'ancestor' or 'founder' in Latin, referring to its status as the most basal pterodactyloid.
rejected.quote: The specific name progenitor means ancestor or founder of a family in Latin, and refers to the animal's status as the most basal member of the Pterodactyloidea.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'The specific name progenitor means ancestor or founder'

rejected.statement: Cladistic analysis shows Kryptodrakon is the sister species to all other known Pterodactyloidea, forming the clade Lophocratia.
rejected.quote: The analysis showed that Kryptodrakon is the sister species of all other known Pterodactyloidea, together forming the Lophocratia, and thus the basalmost pterodactyloid known.
